sources.title: Batch 0062 frozen repository context for binary-tree level-order traversal
Independent Java level-order differential validation against DFS-by-depth oracle

claims.text: The two frozen source occurrences ask for binary-tree level-order traversal and do not prescribe language, node API, null handling or output shape.

Under the declared Java contract, the FIFO implementation with a frozen per-round queue size returns left-to-right values grouped by depth, returns empty for null, and preserves duplicate-valued nodes.
The independently validated implementation covers sparse and wide trees while the answer explicitly distinguishes grouped levels from a flat BFS output and identifies DFS-by-depth as an alternative.

boundary_tests.expected: same left-to-right depth groups as independent DFS-by-depth oracle
all node occurrences preserved in their depth groups

boundary_tests.case: 40,000 seeded random trees up to 90 nodes
boundary_tests.expected: exact match with independent DFS-by-depth oracle

findings: Both frozen primary-source variants ask for binary-tree level-order traversal and are directly covered by the candidate.
The candidate declares its Java node/input/output/null contract instead of presenting unstated source constraints as facts.
The queue invariant is explicit: freeze the pre-round queue size, consume exactly that level, and append non-null children for the next level.
The implementation is runnable and independently revalidated against a DFS-by-depth oracle across fixed sparse/duplicate cases and 40,000 seeded random trees.
Time O(n) and auxiliary queue O(w) bounds are stated with returned output space separated from the queue cost.
The answer covers the one-dimensional-output variant, DFS-by-depth alternative, empty tree, sparse tree, duplicate-value and recursion-stack boundaries without fabricating production experience.
